Implementation Plan

I found the one file to change, so I'm writing the plan now.

## Summary
This is a test-only change. In the `_run_poller` helper in `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`, which starts at line 828, the fake `python3` shim at lines 3462-3464 has its first line hardcoded as `#!/usr/bin/python3`. The plan changes that first line to use the interpreter running the tests (`sys.executable`). The rest of the shim text stays exactly as it is.

Planning ref: `b779077963f7f92dbf2ea37cc9a97d2e2b965815`, branch `main` (not assumed). The `Integration branch mismatch:` line says `unknown`, not `true`, so this is not blocked.

Search results:
- I searched `tests/` for a hardcoded interpreter path (`#!/usr/bin/python3`, plus `#!/usr/bin/python` and `#!/usr/local/bin/python`, excluding `#!/usr/bin/env python...`). The only match is `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py:3464`, so no other test file needs this fix.
- `sys` is imported at module level (line 16), as the issue says.
- The shim text is one raw triple-quoted string running from line 3464 to line 3913.

## Files likely to change
- `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`

## Acceptance
ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py
ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_implement_post_codex_recovery.py
ACCEPTANCE: post-merge none: test-only change to one shim's first line; no workflow, script or runtime behaviour changes

## Functions or modules to implement
- In `_run_poller` (`tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`, line 828), change the second argument of `_write_exec(bin_dir / "python3", ...)` at lines 3462-3464:
  - Before: `r'''#!/usr/bin/python3\nimport json\n...'''`
  - After: `f"#!{sys.executable}\n" + r'''import json\n...'''`
  - That is: remove only `#!/usr/bin/python3` and the line break after it from the start of the raw string, and add the new first line in front by joining two strings with `+`.
  - Keep the raw string as a raw string. Do not make the whole text an f-string: the text contains `{`/`}` characters and `\\n` escapes, and turning it into an f-string would change them.
  - Every line from `import json` (line 3465) to the closing `'''` (line 3913) stays byte-for-byte the same, as does the `_write_exec` helper (line 613).
- No other edits. Assertions, `scripts/render_prompt.py` and `tests/test_render_prompt_foundation.py` stay untouched, as the issue requires.

## Data structures affected
- None. Only the text written to `bin_dir/python3` changes, and only on its first line.

## API or interface changes
- None. `_run_poller`'s parameters and the `REAL_PYTHON_BIN` handling (lines 3261 and 3959) are unchanged. The shim still passes non-mocked calls on to `REAL_PYTHON_BIN` (line 3472).

## Decisions
### D1 — Build the new first line with an f-string and join it to the unchanged raw text
- Chosen: `f"#!{sys.executable}\n" + r'''<existing body without its first line>'''`.
- Alternatives considered: make the whole text an f-string (rejected: braces and escapes would be misread); use `#!/usr/bin/env python3` (rejected: `bin_dir` is first on `PATH`, so `env` would find the shim itself and call it again); replace the first line with `.replace()` when the test runs (rejected: harder to read and depends on the first-line text staying the same).
- Why: this is the smallest edit that leaves the rest of the text byte-for-byte the same, and it is the form the issue suggests.

### D2 — Fix this one file only
- Chosen: edit only line 3464 of `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`.
- Alternatives considered: also change `#!/usr/bin/env python3` shims in other tests, such as `tests/test_implement_post_codex_recovery.py` lines 216, 461, 478 and 866.
- Why: the issue covers only hardcoded `#!/usr/bin/python3` lines, and the search found just this one. The `env` shims already find the right interpreter through `PATH`. Changing them would go beyond the issue (§9).

## Security considerations
- No trust boundary, endpoint, credential or input is touched; the change is local to a test helper.
- `sys.executable` is the path of the Python running the tests, set by the test runner. It is not read from outside input.
- No money handling is involved.

## Potential risks or edge cases
- If `sys.executable` is empty (some embedded interpreters) or its path contains spaces, the first line would be invalid and the shim would fail. Standard CI runners and virtual environments use absolute paths without spaces. No guard is planned; the issue asks for this exact change.
- The shim's first line now points at a fixed absolute path, so it will not find itself again through `bin_dir` on `PATH`; it still calls `REAL_PYTHON_BIN` for real work as before.
- Possible merge conflicts: open PRs #9351, #9134 and #8971 also touch `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`. The edit is one line in a rarely changed area, so the risk is low.
- On runners that have `/usr/bin/python3`, the current code already passes, so the tests are not expected to fail before the change. That is why the done-check has no `red-on-base` marker. The fix matters on runners where `/usr/bin/python3` is missing or differs from the interpreter running the tests.

## Testing considerations
- Run with the installed interpreter: `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py tests/test_implement_post_codex_recovery.py`. Both files must pass. Tests that are skipped because `jq` is missing are not failures.
- Check that the diff touches only one line: `git diff --stat` should show `1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)` (or the same lines rewritten) in `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py` only.
- Run `grep -rn '#!/usr/bin/python3' tests/` again; it should print nothing.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends _write_exec
Scope-mode justification: The issue asks for one exact change: point the shim's first line at the interpreter running the tests, and fix any other test with the same hardcoded line. The search found only one, so the scope stays at one line in one file. The edit keeps using the existing `_write_exec` helper (line 613) and follows the file's own pattern of using `sys.executable` in shims (lines 30695, 31011 and 31386). Following §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), the complete fix and the shortcut are the same edit. No assertion is weakened and no other file changes.

Pre-execution self-check: the target line and file exist on the planning ref; `sys` is imported; there are no other hardcoded `#!/usr/bin/python3` lines in `tests/`; the edit leaves the rest of the shim byte-for-byte unchanged; the excluded files are not touched; nothing needs outside evidence.
